messages:
maya: Quick heads up — the slab handoff patch merged yesterday is tripping a rare double-free during staged compaction. Repro with perf-ci stress (small pages)

sam: Ugh, saw a canary OOM this morning too. Stack points at offload_allocator::commit_handoff() 

jorge: Can you drop the log excerpt? might be the handoff state transition racing with compaction callback

maya: pasted snippet below, it's noisy but you can see the sequence:
```
[2026-03-17T08:12:34Z] handoff: poolA->poolB start id=0x7fae
[2026-03-17T08:12:34Z] compactor: evict_page id=0x7fae
[2026-03-17T08:12:34Z] handoff: poolA->poolB commit id=0x7fae
[2026-03-17T08:12:34Z] compactor: free_page id=0x7fae -> double free
```

katie: Looks like commit and compactor both think they own the page. We need a handoff liveness/invariant or a transient lock. But locks at hot path are scary for perf.

sam: Agree — adding a global lock would hurt. What about a CAS-based state machine on page metadata: STATE {RESIDENT, HANDOFF_IN_PROGRESS, TRANSFERRED, FREE_PENDING} and transitions that make compactor wait briefly or abort if state isn't expected.

jorge: That matches my thought. We already have page->owner and refcount. The bug is that compactor doesn't check the in-progress flag before free. Cheaper fix: compactor does an atomic read of state and if HANDOFF_IN_PROGRESS, it enqueues to a short retry list (bounded retries) rather than freeing. No blocking, just backoff.

maya: Bounded retry seems reasonable. We still need to ensure we don't leak when handoff stalls. A watchdog to flip HANDOFF_IN_PROGRESS -> TRANSFER_FAILED after N ms might be fine.

ops-bot: Reminder: there's an active canary on pool-alpha with the new allocator. Tagging @eng-oncall if needed.

sam: Telemetry question — do we have counts for state-transition failures or handoff stalls? would help calibrate the timeout.

maya: Not yet. I can add counters: handoff_start, handoff_commit, handoff_timeout, handoff_retry_count. Minimal perf overhead if we emit samplers only on debug builds or via runtime flag.

katie: Also add a regression test: stress tight loop of handoff + compaction with randomized sleeps. We had a flaky test like this earlier; make it deterministic by injecting a scheduling point.

jorge: For the state machine, propose the following pseudo:
```
// atomically transition from RESIDENT -> HANDOFF_IN_PROGRESS
if (cmpxchg(&page->state, RESIDENT, HANDOFF_IN_PROGRESS)) {
  // attempt transfer
  if (transfer_ok) {
    page->owner = new_pool;
    page->state = TRANSFERRED; // store-release
  } else {
    page->state = RESIDENT; // rollback
  }
} else {
  // someone else racing: compactor or other handoff
}
```
Compactor should only free when cmpxchg TRANSFERRED -> FREE_PENDING succeeds. If HANDOFF_IN_PROGRESS, push to retry queue.

sam: Sounds good. We should also audit other code paths that touch page->owner to ensure they do cmpxchg and honor states.

maya: Action items: 1) I'll add the state enum + atomic transitions and counters behind a runtime flag (maya/handshake-saga-flag). 2) Jorge to add deterministic stress test in alloc-tests. 3) Katie to add telemetry dashboard query for handoff_timeout and retry spikes. 4) Sam to run canary with flag on pool-alpha.

katie: ETA?

maya: PR this week for the atomic states + tests. Will gate by flag. If canary looks stable, roll to staging next week.

sam: One more thought — we might be able to make handoff idempotent so duplicate commits are no-ops; that reduces races. But that needs careful refcount semantics. Follow up RFC maybe.

jorge: Agreed. Let's do the atomic state patch first (low risk), then RFC for idempotent handoffs as a longer-term refactor.

maya: I'll draft a short RFC draft after the patch lands, focusing on idempotency model, refcount invariants, and perf model.

ops-bot: Deploy check: perf-ci run queued (job 4521).

sam: Thanks all. Ping me if you need help with the canary rollout or rollback hooks. :thumbsup:
